perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals

factors.name: channelDiversification
factors.basis: Serve announced an August 17 launch on Grubhub beginning with more than 100 participating merchants in Chicago and nearly 200 in Los Angeles, adding another delivery marketplace alongside existing channels.

risks: Merchant availability does not establish order density, revenue per robot or profitable utilization.
unknowns: Incremental order volume, take rate and unit economics from Grubhub were not disclosed.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution

factors.name: fleetUtilizationInitiatives
factors.basis: The same announcement described expansion to San Jose and Washington, DC, a Miami micro-depot, a merchant hardware product and advertising services as utilization initiatives.

risks: Multiple simultaneous initiatives increase execution complexity while Q2 guidance already showed demand-conversion risk.
contradictions: Network/channel expansion is constructive but does not by itself resolve the lower Uber Eats volume that drove the Q2 guidance cut.
unknowns: Contribution of each initiative to 2026 revenue and fleet utilization remains unknown.

sources.origin: Serve Robotics Investor Relations / Grubhub and network expansion announcement
facts: Serve launched robot delivery on Grubhub with more than 100 participating merchants in Chicago and nearly 200 in Los Angeles.
Serve also announced expansion to San Jose and Washington, DC, a Miami micro-depot, a merchant hardware product and advertising service.

result: Distinct primary-source channel and utilization evidence packaged for Alpha; it does not resolve the prior guidance contradiction and numeric underwriting remains Alpha-owned.
